claim.quote: which yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations, thus providing direct observation of the Higgs boson decay into b-quarks.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as Phys. Lett. B 786 (2018) 59.

name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

significance.quote: an observed (expected) significance of 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations

summary.plain: ATLAS saw the Higgs boson decaying into bottom quarks - its single most common decay - by looking for it alongside a W or Z boson.
summary.technical: VH production, H -> bb, using 79.8 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV results: observed (expected) significance 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations.

title: Observation of H -> bbbar decays and VH production with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: H -> bb is the dominant Higgs decay mode; observing it at the predicted rate confirmed the Standard Model coupling of the Higgs boson to down-type quarks.
